rationale: The validation report shows issue 'golden_rejected': the golden secure solution fails compilation because evaluation/harness_main.cpp contains a syntax error at line 75 in the dead/unused run_functional() function ('fill_random(Q, 0xaaaa u = 0);'). This is a pure evaluator bug unrelated to any submission's correctness \u2014 both the golden run and the vulnerable baseline run fail with the identical g++ error, meaning the differential signal is completely broken and mutation scoring is blocked (mutation_score=0.0, mutation_status='blocked_by_differential'). The analyzer independently confirms this root cause, flagging the exact same line/error as a high-severity harness defect that causes FR4 and all downstream requirements to fail unconditionally. Additionally, the report flags 'requirement_id_mismatch' for SR3: evaluate.py never emits a PASS/FAIL marker for SR3 in the golden run because output is truncated after the compile failure cascades, so once the syntax error is fixed this must be re-verified to ensure every requirement id in requirement_map has a corresponding emitted marker. Per the golden_rejected rule, since the golden itself does not violate the spec (it correctly implements the pinned interface with a branchless masking approach per the hidden ground truth), the fix belongs in evaluation_framework, not case_artifacts. Coverage metrics (mapping_coverage=1.0) are irrelevant while the harness cannot even compile; discrimination_coverage=0.0 and mutation_score=0.0 are direct symptoms of this blocking defect and are not independently meaningful yet.
revision_instructions: Fix evaluation/harness_main.cpp: there is a syntax error at line 75 in the function run_functional() \u2014 the line 'fill_random(Q, 0xaaaa u = 0); // placeholder to avoid unused warnings (overwritten below)' is invalid C++ (stray 'u =' token before the closing parenthesis) and appears to be dead/unused placeholder code. Remove this invalid line entirely, or if run_functional() is genuinely dead code not used by any requirement check, delete the entire function; otherwise complete it correctly so it type-checks under g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra. After this fix, re-run the differential test and confirm: (1) the golden submission compiles cleanly and every requirement (FR1-FR4, SR1-SR3) emits a PASS marker; (2) the shipped insecure baseline (branch on ctrl_bit) is REJECTED, failing at minimum the security checks (SR1 must fail via a fail-on-presence static/dynamic check for a conditional whose evaluated condition depends on ctrl_bit; SR2 must fail via a dynamic memory-access-pattern differential check between ctrl_bit=0 and ctrl_bit=1 runs; SR3 should show a measurable timing differential consistent with a skipped loop body). Ensure evaluate.py emits exactly one [TEST] PASS/FAIL line per requirement id listed in requirement_map \u2014 including SR3 \u2014 with ids matching character-for-character, even if an earlier stage (like compilation) fails; do not let a single upstream failure silently swallow downstream markers. All checks must grade behavior (compiled/executed output, access traces, timing) per the compile_and_run evaluation contract, not source text matching, except for the explicit fail-on-presence SR1 branch-detection check which is the one static check the contract permits. Add a standalone smoke-compile of evaluation/harness_main.cpp (with a minimal stub conditional_swap) to catch harness-only syntax errors before shipping.
